text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a 3x 95th-percentile tail in us-east1 GPU pool (pool-1) over the last 6m. CPU on the host is fine but PCIe error counters spiked on host-42. Suspect cross-tenant DMA storms / noisy neighbor. cc @maria :eyes:

maria: ugh, yep saw the alert. Is this impacting dedicated slices or only shared?

alex: Mostly shared slices (fractional). Dedicated tenants look okay. Throughput drop ~18% for small-gen workloads.

jon: can you paste the host counters? did the NIC fifo overflow too?

alex: logs clipped: ```host=host-42 pci_err=15 nvlink_retries=120 nic_drop=3```. Also noticed hbm-eviction spikes in the same 30s windows.

maria: hbm evict + nvlink retries = bad combo. Could be a kernel driver regression or a tenant doing heavy kv cache churn. Any tenant IDs in allocation logs?

alex: tenant_988 and tenant_101 have a big bump in sustained small-token QPS during the window. Routing shows they were colocated on the same shelf.

jon: ok. immediate mitigation options: 1) migrate tenant_988 off host-42 (hot-handoff) 2) apply soft-fence: nic egress shaping for tenant_101 3) promote to dedicated pool for both (costly)

sre_liz: we tried hot-handoff earlier and saw 10s pause on warmup. For low-latency customers that pause is worse than degraded throughput. Soft-fence seems safest short-term.

maria: agree. What's the cost / perf delta for soft-fence? We need numbers to present to pricing.

jon: rough numbers from last sim: shaping to 60% egress reduces interference and restores 95th to baseline for neighbors, increases token p99 for the shaped tenant by ~12% and increases infra CPU on proxy by ~4%. No change to billing.

alex: i'm going to apply a temporary soft-fence and move tenant_988 to a different shelf. Patch: ```kubectl annotate alloc tenant=tenant_101 infra/shaping=egress=60% --context=us-east1```

ops-bot: action queued: apply egress shaping to allocation 988/101 on host-42. ETA 12s.

sre_liz: after shaping, telemetry looks better. 95th back to baseline within 90s. HBM evicts dropped to normal. nvlink retries down to single digits. Nice.

maria: great. Longer-term action items: - run forensic kernel/driver checks on host-42 - add allocation affinity check to scheduler to avoid heavy kv-churn colocations - price team: evaluate a new "isolation-tune" add-on (soft-fence SLA) to charge for shaping/operational overhead

jon: +1 on scheduler rule. Also consider a low-friction dedicated-slice trial for tenants hitting this pattern (auto-upgrade to burst-dedicated with minute-level billing).

alex: filing followups: github issue with kernel traces (link), scheduler task to add affinity rule, and a PR to the billing runway for isolation-tune pricing proposal.

maria: thanks all. tagging for postmortem if recurrence: @sre_liz @jon. :thumbsup:
